implementationNotes: Catch log remains the inner Collection > Pokédex > Catch log destination, not a new root page.
Rows represent individual records, preserving duplicate species and stable entry IDs. Counts and filters measure individuals, while the Pokédex measures species.
Match the existing ordering: pin the active raising record first; sort historical entries by recorded time newest first. Unknown legacy dates remain unknown, never invented, and follow dated history.
Keep rarity and shiny filters available while the list scrolls. Preserve Uncommon and Legendary choices even though this illustrative set has zero of each.
Use one filter interface: do not copy the first generated image's redundant Rarity/Shiny dropdowns alongside the count chips.
Rarity, nature, recorded time, raising/trophy/released state and evolution order come from actual entry data. Mock fixture values are illustrative.
Released is a historical state, not a new Release action. This page introduces no training, item use, trading, deletion, export or manual logging controls.
Selecting a record updates its preview only. View details must open the existing detail experience for that exact individual, not just the first matching species.
Correct shiny sprites and accessible Shiny labels must use the entry's isShiny data; incidental generated sprite colours are not the implementation target.
All essential record data and navigation remain available with optional extras hidden.
Preserve existing empty collection and zero-filter-result states, stable scroll behaviour and loading/unknown metadata handling.
Keep approved sidebar/major section boundaries line-free, regardless of incidental local strokes in generated references.
